entries.title: Ukrainian drones target St Petersburg in attack Russia calls 'unprecedented'
entries.snippet: The city's governor urges residents to remain indoors for the first time since the beginning of the war.

entries.title: US and Iran exchange strikes in Gulf in latest test of ceasefire
entries.snippet: The US military says it struck Iranian drones and radar sites. Tehran responds by targeting US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain.

entries.title: Armenia braces for election as Russia piles pressure on pro-West government
entries.snippet: Incumbent Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan is seeking a third term despite falling domestic support.

entries.title: Lebanon says three soldiers killed in Israeli attack on car
entries.snippet: The Israeli military is investigating the incident in south Lebanon, where it is fighting Hezbollah.

entries.title: Iran says staff blocked from entering US after players given World Cup visas
entries.snippet: Iranian officials say technical staff have been denied visas, hours after the US said players could enter the country.

entries.title: Man dies after bitten by shark in Western Australia, police say
entries.snippet: The man was spearfishing off Michaelmas Island with his family, according to local reports.

entries.title: Tributes to Buffy and Ted Lasso star Anthony Head after death aged 72
entries.snippet: The British actor, who also appeared in Merlin and Little Britain, died of complications from pneumonia.

entries.title: Rumours and speculation as fans forecast date of Taylor Swift's wedding
entries.snippet: Swifties worldwide are looking for clues about the superstar's nuptials to American football star Travis Kelce.

entries.title: Canada bans Texas cattle over flesh-eating screwworm outbreak in US
entries.snippet: The ban came as a second infected calf was identified in Texas, and the US state declaring a state of disaster over the outbreak.

entries.title: Palestinian baby killed by Israeli gunfire in West Bank, health ministry says
entries.snippet: The Israeli military says Friday's "incident is under review", expressing "deep sorrow for any harm caused".

entries.title: Nearly 50 people die of thirst in Sahara desert after lorry breaks down
entries.snippet: Only two survived after trekking more than 50km (30 miles) across the desert to alert the authorities.

entries.title: Putin says there is 'no point' meeting Zelensky over ending Ukraine war
entries.snippet: The Russian president's refusal comes after his Ukrainian counterpart wrote an open letter calling for face-to-face talks.

entries.title: US stocks slump as fears over Big Tech shake Wall Street
entries.snippet: The Nasdaq saw its biggest daily fall since early 2025.

entries.title: Ukraine strikes cargo ships and admits Romania drone blast
entries.snippet: Ukraine says it struck five ships carrying illegal cargo in the Sea of Azov and in coastal waters of Russian-occupied territories.

entries.title: Astronauts return to ISS after sheltering during air leak repair attempt
entries.snippet: Russian attempt to repair tunnel area sparks safe-haven procedure for five other astronauts onboard.

entries.title: Norway's crown princess on lung transplant waiting list, palace says
entries.snippet: Mette-Marit's condition, which stiffens the lungs, making it hard to breathe, has deteriorated, the royal household says.

entries.title: I wanted to quit Eurovision twice - then won it, says Bangaranga singer Dara
entries.snippet: The Bulgarian singer says her historic victory in Vienna came close to never happening.

entries.title: Fury in France after child murder suspect's criminal record released
entries.snippet: A man suspected of murdering an 11-year-old girl had previously been identified as a potential child molester, records show.

entries.title: US actor James Handy stabbed to death, with girlfriend's son arrested
entries.snippet: Handy, 81, is known for his roles in films including Jumanji and Top Gun: Maverick.

entries.title: Three jailed over heist of ancient golden helmet from Dutch museum
entries.snippet: The men are sentenced to 47 months each for stealing the 2,500-year-old Romanian Coțofenești helmet.

entries.title: A park famed for rare gorillas gears up to fight Ebola and protect its primates
entries.snippet: In Virunga National Park, rangers are on the front lines — playing a critical role to contain the surging virus while coping with an upsurge in conflict-related violence.

entries.title: Israeli airstrikes kill 9 including Lebanese army officers after ceasefire deal
entries.snippet: The Israeli military confirmed hitting a vehicle and said the incident is being reviewed. Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun called the strike "a flagrant violation to Lebanese sovereignty and international law."

entries.title: Filipino sailors say they were falsely accused of possessing child porn and deported
entries.snippet: NPR has tracked deported Filipino sailors who say they were accused without evidence of possessing child sexual exploitation material. Almost none have been charged or prosecuted.

entries.title: Peru is set to elect its 10th president in a decade
entries.snippet: Peruvians will elect their new president Sunday with polls suggesting a polarized but tight race between hard-right candidate Keiko Fujimori and leftist Roberto Sánchez.

entries.title: In Ohio, the Sikh community passes traditions to the next generation
entries.snippet: Photographer Akash Pamarthy has documented the Sikh religious community in Ohio over several years. His photos tell a story.

entries.title: The Forest Service says it's closing offices to cut costs. But the math doesn't add up
entries.snippet: The Forest Service is trying to shut down research hubs because it says it needs to live within its means. But the agency plans to close facilities that cost less than $1 to rent while keeping open one that costs $1 million.

entries.title: Knicks beat Spurs by one point for 2-0 lead in NBA Finals
entries.snippet: The red-hot Knicks are going home, two wins away from an NBA championship that the capital of the world has been waiting to see for generations.

entries.title: U.S. military says it shot down Iranian drones launched toward Gulf allies
entries.snippet: The exchange of strikes comes as the Trump administration ramps up pressure on Iran to make a deal to end the conflict.

entries.title: Democrat Xavier Becerra wins the top spot in November's race for California governor
entries.snippet: Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra has clinched the top spot on California's ballot for governor. With millions of ballots still to be counted, his November challenger is unknown.

entries.title: After D.C.'s Reflecting Pool gets repainted, visitors ask: What changed?
entries.snippet: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is refilling after President Trump had it painted "American flag blue." Some visitors say the results of the project — which reportedly cost millions — are subtle.

entries.title: Trump says he wants Pulte to further slash staffing at national intelligence office
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump said Friday that he wants his new acting director of national intelligence, Bill Pulte, to cut the office, which has already been significantly scaled back during his second term.

entries.title: Why hiring surged in May despite economic strain from the Iran war
entries.snippet: There was surprising strength in the latest U.S. jobs report. Employers added 172,000 jobs in May, the third straight month of job gains. Overall, the labor market appears strong despite concerns about the Iran war, rising prices and artificial intelligence. Amna Nawaz speaks wit

entries.title: What may happen as oil supplies dwindle and Strait of Hormuz remains mostly closed
entries.snippet: As U.S.-Iran talks show little sign of progress, commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains sharply reduced, raising concerns about global energy markets and supply chains. Geoff Bennett speaks with energy analyst Daniel Yergin, vice chairman of S&P Global, for more

entries.title: News Wrap: Senate passes $70 billion immigration enforcement bill
entries.snippet: In our news wrap Friday, Senate Republicans passed a $70 billion bill to fund immigration enforcement, Trump said he wants his new acting director of national intelligence to slash the agency's staffing, a federal judge struck down the Trump administration's immigration processin

entries.title: What Putin's rejection of Ukraine's call for talks means for efforts to end Russia's war
entries.snippet: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy is accusing Russia of choosing war over peace, after Russian President Putin rejected his request for an in-person meeting. Putin spoke at an annual economic forum in St. Petersburg, a city on edge after several Ukrainian airstrikes earlier this week

entries.title: Brooks and Capehart on some Republican lawmakers' defiance of Trump
entries.snippet: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Amna Nawaz to discuss the week in politics, including Republican defiance of President Donald Trump and fresh scandals in a key Senate race.

entries.title: Art exhibit shines light on women's role in technologies that power modern life
entries.snippet: Women have played a vital role in building the technologies that shape modern life, but their contributions have at times been overlooked, minimized or left out of the historical record. A new art exhibition seeks to tell a fuller story. Special correspondent Mike Cerre reports f

entries.title: This chef will teach you how to make healthy $5 family dinners
entries.snippet: With rising grocery prices, many Americans are struggling to provide healthy, complete meals for their families. One chef is teaching his TikTok followers how to eat well on a budget, one $5 meal at a time. Deema Zein reports.

entries.title: Energy Department says advanced nuclear reactor first to reach critical milestone
entries.snippet: The milestone occurs when a nuclear reactor achieves a self-sustaining chain reaction capable of producing a steady release of energy.

entries.title: As states face stricter Medicaid work requirements, Nebraska is an early test
entries.snippet: Millions are likely to lose coverage as states begin complying with the new federal rules.

entries.title: Trump's deportation agenda is about to get a $70B infusion from Congress
entries.snippet: For those aligned with Trump's campaign promise for the largest mass deportation operation in U.S. history, it all but guarantees an uninterrupted flow of money to carry out the administration's immigration enforcement operations — and comes on top of some $170 billion Congress a

entries.title: WATCH: Trump holds roundtable with farmers in Wisconsin
entries.snippet: "We love the farmers, we love everything about your state," President Donald Trump told his audience at a rally being held in a barn in Chippewa Falls, Wisconsin, on Friday.

entries.title: U.S. job market is strong, but many Americans still frustrated by prospects and rising prices
entries.snippet: With just five months to go before consequential midterm elections in the U.S., Americans have grown increasingly frustrated by rising costs, and it's unclear if the strong job numbers this year will change their gloomy view of the economy.

entries.title: Trump's troop reversals in Europe could cost taxpayers millions, officials say
entries.snippet: The U.S. military is waiting for clarity from the Pentagon following President Donald Trump's back-and-forth on troop levels in Europe, upending the lives of military personnel and potentially costing taxpayers millions of dollars, two U.S. defense officials told The Associated P

entries.title: Judge strikes down Trump policy that halted asylum decisions for 39 countries
entries.snippet: A federal judge on Friday struck down a Trump administration policy enacted after the shooting of two National Guard members that made it harder for immigrants from dozens of countries to stay and enter the U.S.

entries.title: What to know about the New World screwworm fly and its U.S. reappearance
entries.snippet: The New World screwworm fly is threatening the $113 billion U.S. cattle industry for the first time in more than a half century, with an infestation from its flesh-eating larvae confirmed in south Texas.

entries.title: Anthony Head, British actor known for 'Buffy the Vampire Slayer,' dies at 72
entries.snippet: Head achieved U.S. fame as librarian Rupert Giles, mentor to the title character in the cult-favorite supernatural series "Buffy the Vampire Slayer," which ran from 1997 to 2003.

entries.title: Former Prince Andrew made money subletting cottages on his rent-free estate, report shows
entries.snippet: The National Audit Office report said Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor received income from renting out the cottages on the Royal Lodge estate, his home near Windsor Castle for more than 20 years. A lease for Royal Lodge signed in 2003 shows he paid only a nominal fee known as a "peppe

entries.title: Treasury warns banks of 'red flags' tied to customers in the U.S. illegally
entries.snippet: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network — also known a FinCEN — issued an advisory Friday to banks that tells them to watch out for identity theft, payroll tax fraud, and money laundering schemes tied to hiring unauthorized workers.

entries.title: Graham Platner to hold Maine rally with Rep. Ro Khanna as scandals shake up campaign
entries.snippet: Last weekend, his campaign wrestled with stories about sexually explicit messages that Platner sent to several women while he was married. Then on Thursday, The New York Times reported about his relationships with previous girlfriends. Some viewed him positively but others descri

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Germany news: Teen Karl to miss World Cup through injury
entries.snippet: Bayern Munich's 18-year-old midfielder Lennart Karl sustained an injury during training in Chicago. Meanwhile, politically-motivated crimes have doubled in a decade, according to a newspaper report. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Man killed in shark attack off Western Australia
entries.snippet: A diver has died after an attack by a suspected 4.5-meter shark near Michaelmas Island. It is the third fatal ‌shark attack ⁠in ⁠Australia in three weeks.

entries.title: India news: 'Cockroach' party holds protest at Jantar Mantar
entries.snippet: "Cockroach" party founder Abhijeet Dipke is demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Meanwhile, India has named teen Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in its latest T20 squad. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: Fujimori or Sanchez? Peru vote marks 10 years of turmoil
entries.snippet: Sunday's presidential runoff in Peru pits Keiko Fujimori against Roberto Sanchez in an election marked by social tension, rising crime and declining confidence in political institutions.

entries.title: Pope Leo to focus on immigration, social justice in Spain
entries.snippet: Pope Leo XIV begins a weeklong trip to Spain, turning papal attention back to Europe and its Christian roots. The pope will also meet with some victims of sexual abuse by Catholic clergy.

entries.title: As hot summer, blackouts loom, Iraq looks to solar power
entries.snippet: With so much sunlight, Iraq is very well-positioned to use solar power to help fix its annual summer electricity crisis. So why is it that Iraq's government has only recently started to take solar power seriously?

entries.title: Hantavirus: Scientists head to western Argentina to trace outbreak source
entries.snippet: Argentine and US scientists will test rodents in Mendoza as investigators try to trace the source of a hantavirus outbreak that killed three people.

entries.title: Middle East: Iran says it targeted US bases in Gulf
entries.snippet: Kuwait reported intercepting drones while Bahrain sounded air-raid sirens. This came after the United States said it shot down Iranian drones and attacked radar sites. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: Nigeria, Ghana offer to help citizens leave South Africa
entries.snippet: The governments of Nigeria and Ghana are offering to fly citizens home from South Africa after a spate of anti-migrant attacks.

entries.title: EU leaders at Balkan summit optimistic about rapid expansion
entries.snippet: German Chancellor Merz has said he wants Western Balkan countries to be better integrated into the EU as they seek full membership. Commission head Von der Leyen called for a "faster" enlargement process.

entries.title: Germany's Iran war lessons after 100 days
entries.snippet: The war waged by the US and Israel against Iran has now lasted 100 days. In that time, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has drastically changed his stance on the war.

entries.title: Finland: 4 suspects in sabotage of undersea cable link with Estonia
entries.snippet: Police say they have four suspects, three of whom face travel bans, after investigations into the sabotage of two telecommunications cables under the Baltic Sea in late 2025. Prosecutors will decide on the next steps.

entries.title: How disinformation in Congo is worsening Ebola epidemic
entries.snippet: The deadly Ebola outbreak isn't the only thing causing concern for health workers in Congo. Rumors and disinformation are hindering efforts to contain the virus. The patterns are well-known — and could be confronted.

entries.title: North Korea quietly ramps up its nuclear program
entries.snippet: With Washington's attention elsewhere, North Korea has slowly been building up its nuclear weapons program. This week, Kim Jong Un took a publicity tour of a new nuclear fuel facility while promising to build more bombs.

entries.title: Ethiopia: An election without a real challenge?
entries.snippet: Ethiopia's ruling Prosperity Party is set for a decisive election win despite security challenges, a divided opposition and some regions not voting.

entries.title: Successive elections take a hit on Kosovo's coffers
entries.snippet: Sunday's election in Kosovo — the third in under 16 months — is marked by a clash between former allies PM Albin Kurti and ex-President Vjosa Osmani, deadlock in the dialogue with Serbia, and obstacles to EU integration.

entries.title: Why businesses are offering 'Quiet Hour'
entries.snippet: More peace and quiet, less stress — the Quiet Hour is an initiative for people with invisible disabilities. An increasing number of stores and institutions in Germany are launching similar campaigns.

entries.title: Iran at war: Stability masks deepening crises
entries.snippet: One hundred days after the start of the Iran war, the Islamic Republic appears stable. But beneath the surface, economic strain, social unrest and growing repression point to deeper instability.

entries.title: US Senate passes $70 billion funding for ICE, Border Patrol
entries.snippet: Senators voted 52-47 to approve funds to finance the immigration forces for another three years, through the rest of Donald Trump's term. The bill still needs to clear the House; that vote is expected next week.
